purpose: The surface a dashboard tile or a block of page content sits on — a bordered box with an optional heading row.

useInstead.when: you only need spacing between things
useInstead.use: Stack — does this content need a visible surface, or just breathing room?

useInstead.when: it is the page's own container

useInstead.use: a dialog or Menu — a Card does not float or trap focus

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for Card decisions in this package.

rules.because: it renders a consistently-sized <h3> in a header row; a hand-written heading inside children gets neither

rules.if: the tile needs a control beside its name — a menu, a filter, a link
rules.because: it sits at the header's right edge, vertically centred against the title
the inner gap is spacing.2 (8px) against 16px between cards — one step down the same scale, saying that things inside a card are more related to each other than two cards are

constraints: The title is always an <h3>. There is no `titleAs` override, because a generator choosing heading levels per tile is how a page ends up jumping from h1 to h5.
Card sets no margins. Spacing between cards is the parent Stack's or Grid's gap.

composition.childrenContract: Any content. Children are laid out as a flex column with the card's gap between them.
composition.notes: Cards nest legally but rarely should — two borders inside each other read as a mistake more often than as a hierarchy.

antiPatterns.dont: Writing <h2> or <h3> inside children instead of passing `title`
antiPatterns.why: the header row gives you consistent size, weight and alignment with `actions`; a hand-written heading gets none of it and will not match the next card

antiPatterns.dont: Adding margin-bottom to a Card to separate it from the next one
antiPatterns.do: Let the parent Stack or Grid supply the gap
antiPatterns.why: margin adds to the gap, so the rhythm drifts from 16px wherever someone remembered to add it

antiPatterns.dont: Nesting Cards to group content inside a tile
antiPatterns.do: Use a Stack, or a heading and a divider
antiPatterns.why: two nested borders read as an accident; the inner grouping does not need a surface of its own

antiPatterns.dont: Overriding padding to a raw value for one tile
antiPatterns.do: Pass a token from the spacing scale, or leave it
antiPatterns.why: a raw value escapes the scale and that one card stops matching every other
